first.rationale: Two of the three current pressures are internal funnel decay (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a single onboarding intervention plausibly moves both. memory_86 is the load-bearing record for that choice, so it is the first verification target: its summary reports completion rate and time-to-value gains, which are early proxies, not the long-term qualified revenue this objective is scored on. I need the source record to see the measurement window, whether retention or expansion was tracked past week one, and whether 'shortening' removed steps that establish product value. memory_31 (signup field reduction) is a consistent but distinct intervention and is not sufficient on its own. The second verification target is memory_73, because competitor entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the most tempting alternative and it is the direction where an unverified summary is most dangerous: discount-led acquisition reliably shows strong acquisition and revenue lift on short horizons while degrading the quality and durability of the acquired base, which is exactly the failure mode this objective penalizes. If the memory_73 record shows a long horizon with retention and margin held, I would reconsider; if it shows a short window and headline acquisition numbers, that direction is disqualified rather than merely deprioritized. Explicit downstream risk on my own choice: 'shorter onboarding' can raise completion by deferring the work that produces a genuinely activated account, converting a real funnel problem into a better-looking metric. I therefore intend a standard experiment instrumented on downstream qualified revenue and 30/60-day retention, not on completion rate alone, with a stop condition if completion rises while first meaningful action or retention falls. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) and referral_incentive (memory_57) address neither current deficit and are held. memory_91 remains the fallback if verification undercuts memory_86.
